dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: I can't keep working here. Maybe I should try relocating to Romaritime Harbor?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why can't you stay in Lumidouce Harbor?

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: Ah, right. You're not working here, so you probably don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: This place is far from the Court of Fontaine, and we're not exactly swimming in choices for shops or recreation of any kind, really. There's only one tavern, but I'm not a big drinker.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: In any case, I wish you a pleasant stay in Lumidouce Harbor. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: I can't really go to Romaritime Harbor. It's directly adjacent to the desert, and my friend who works there told me that the wind is always blowing in a bunch of sand.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: If I get blasted by that wind for too long, my skin would surely become a grotesque horror show.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: I suppose if all else fails, I can always look for a job back in the city...

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: Mr. Doutey is a good guy. He's really diligent and friendly, and always puts others first.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: Having said that, the man is a bit too obsessed with reports, data sheets, and meeting minutes.

dialogues.speaker: Jalade
dialogues.text: I half-suspect the main reason he proposed to expand Lumidouce Harbor was so that he could immerse himself in a deluge of meetings every day.
